newsitem.title: USA: Ikon Office tumbles after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Ikon Office tumbles after profit warning.

text.p: Shares in Ikon Office Solutions Inc fell more than 26 percent on Friday after the company warned that its earnings for its fiscal third and fourth quarters would not meet analysts' expectations.
Salomon Brothers analyst Jonathan Rosenzweig downgraded his rating on the stock to hold from strong buy, saying the news "seriously damaged" his confidence in the company for the time being.
Lehman Brothers analyst Phua Young advised investors in a research note to wait for the "dust to settle" before buying into the stock.
Ikon was off 8-3/8 to 23-5/8 in New York Stock Exchange trading.
"Yesterday's events are just one more in a series of disappointments and credibility issues which have surfaced over the last 12 months," Rosenzweig said in a report.
"Although the stock may look cheap, one cannot help but think that there could be other hurdles near term as Ikon embarks on its transformation," the Salomon analyst added.
Ikon has embarked on a "transformation" program aimed at lowering its administrative costs and improving its margins.
The company linked its earnings shortfall to issues related to the acceleration of the transformationn program.

"We failed to recognize the temporary strain the transformation would put on sales growth in our traditional copier business," John Stuart, Ikon's chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement.

Rosenzweig cut his fiscal 1997 earnings per share estimate on the company to a range of $1.35-$1.40 before transformation charges from a prior $1.55. His 1998 estimate dropped to a $1.60-$1.70 range before charges from $2.10.
